newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: After fluctuating between positive and negative territory for most of the session on Tuesday, Dutch bonds ended higher.
Dealers said trade was thin, increasing volatility.
"There's a genuine weakness in the market," one dealer said.
He said the Bund market should find support from Tietmeyer's comments made late on Monday on a possible EMU delay, should big countries miss the convergence criteria.
"It means they won't sacrifice everything on behalf of the Euro," the dealer said.
But dealers said the Bund market would be pressured by the uncertain outcome of the French snap elections announced yesterday evening and to be held on March 25 and June 1.
"A Chirac victory is not guaranteed. And if he does win, you never know what his policy will come down to exactly," one said.
He added the overload of statements concerning EMU had led to a kind of overkill on news in this field.
"People don't look seriously at it anymore. Each day, we have several BUBA and other comments on it (EMU). In principle, the market no longer trades on it very much," he said.
The government issued five billion marks of the bond in a first tranche, and a second tranche will be sold in an auction on Wednesday.
The first tranche was sold at a fixed price of 101.45 for a yield of 5.80 percent, and the entire issue is expected to total about 15 billion marks.
